absent: Complete remainder of task_numa_migrate node scan loop and its final selection and return handling beyond the truncated fragment.
Definitions and defaults for scan and fault helpers such as task_scan_min, group_faults_shared, group_faults_priv, group_faults, task_weight, group_weight and task_faults_idx.
Semantics and defaults for promotion helpers and tunables not fully shown such as promo_wmark_pages, sysctl_numa_balancing_mode, sysctl_numa_balancing_promote_rate_limit and tiering flags.
Exact run queue, task, zone and pglist_data layouts and the meaning of counters such as nr_numa_running, nr_preferred_running and numa_migrate_on beyond their uses here.
Scheduler domain imbalance fields and adjust_numa_imbalance helper behavior used to discount movement imbalance.
Idle and capacity helpers such as is_core_idle, idle_cpu, sched_smt_active, cpu_load, cpu_runnable, cpu_util_cfs and capacity_of.

findings.text: NUMA balancing exposes globally visible tunables for minimum scan period, maximum scan period, scan size, scan delay and hot threshold that other parts of the kernel can read and administrators can adjust.
Default minimum scan period is 1000 and default maximum scan period is 60000.
Default scan size is 256 and default scan delay is 1000.
Default hot threshold is initialized from the milliseconds per second constant.
Maximum scan window bound is 2560.
Hint fault accounting defines two fault types, four type direction statistics, and eight buckets derived by successive doubling.
Active node comparison factor is 3.
Promotion threshold adjustment uses 16 discrete steps.
Minimum meaningful NUMA improvement threshold is 30.
Enumerator node_has_spare has value zero with later states taking successive values.

Structure numa_group contains refcount for lifetime, lock for membership, nr_tasks for population, gid for identity, active_nodes for spread, rcu for deferred free, total_faults and max_faults_cpu for aggregates, plus trailing faults counters split between memory and processor regions with processor region weighted toward affinity.

Structure numa_stats aggregates load, runnable, util, compute_capacity, nr_running, weight, node_type and idle_cpu to characterize demand versus capacity plus a cached idle processor where negative denotes none.

Search context task_numa_env binds p, src_cpu, src_nid, dst_cpu, dst_nid, imb_numa_nr, src_stats, dst_stats, imbalance_pct, dist, best_task, best_imp and best_cpu to track migrating task, endpoints, summaries, tolerance, distance and best candidate.

Node condition advances among node_has_spare, node_fully_busy and node_overloaded where spare denotes capacity to accept work, fully busy denotes full use without contention for cycles, and overloaded denotes inability to meet expected cycles.
Membership lock inside the NUMA group serializes updates to task population while lifetime is managed by reference counting with deferred reclamation.

Group pointers, scheduling domain pointers, shared balance flags and run queue current tasks are observed under read side critical sections with dereference helpers that require the corresponding unlock, tolerating concurrent migration and update.

Per run queue migration flag coordinates competing placement attempts through atomic exchange with single access reads and writes, allowing fallback to another idle processor when the first choice is already claimed and clearing the previous best when superseded.
Initial scan delay is at least a task specific minimum and grows with shared memory pressure scaled by group size and the proportion of shared faults to total faults.
Enqueue accounting increments per run queue NUMA counters when the task has a valid preferred node and additionally when that preference matches the current node.
Per node CPU fault total is the sum of its two directional buckets and a node counts as active when that total scaled by the configured fraction exceeds the group peak.
Combined processor identifier is considered valid only when its decoded processor number lies within the configured processor range.
A memory node is deemed to have ample free space when any populated zone satisfies its promotion watermark plus a margin derived from total present pages bounded below by a gigabyte equivalent.
Hint fault latency exchanges the stored access timestamp for the current millisecond time and returns the masked difference, tolerating wrap.
Promotion candidacy counting throttles when the number of candidates observed within a one second window reaches the configured rate bound, with window start advanced atomically.
Hotness threshold adapts once per maximum scan period by comparing recent candidate volume against expected volume with ten percent tolerance, stepping the threshold up or down within bounded limits.

Global predicate decides whether a page should migrate toward a destination processor based on tiering latency and rate controls for access timed pages and on identity, lifetime, group affinity and hysteresis weighted fault ratios otherwise, refusing memoryless targets.

Migration is favored early in task lifetime for first or private faults, always allowed for private reuse, and otherwise requires stronger destination affinity shown through group CPU dominance or capacity weighted fault proportions with hysteresis.
Node classification compares running count against CPU weight and capacity normalized utilization and runnable pressure against a percentage tolerance to select spare, busy or overloaded.
Idle core selection prefers an idle physical core over hyperthread siblings when simultaneous multithreading is active and the shared domain reports idle cores, otherwise retaining any prior choice.

Node statistics collection zeroes the summary, accumulates load, runnable, utilization, running count and capacity across online processors of the node, derives weight and category, and caches a usable idle processor favoring whole cores.

Best candidate recording claims the destination run queue, seeks an alternative idle allowed processor when already claimed, releases any superseded claim, and transfers task references to the new best.
Imbalance test normalizes source and destination loads by their respective capacities and reports worsening when the proposed absolute gap exceeds the original gap.

Pairwise placement evaluation combines task or group fault differentials with preferred node bonuses and penalties, suppresses tiny gains, enforces load balance and affinity constraints, handles idle destinations, and signals when further search is unlikely to help.

Destination search allows direct moves to idle processors when spare capacity shows no adjusted imbalance or when load comparison permits, otherwise scanning allowed processors for beneficial swaps until told to stop.

Top level NUMA placement derives tolerance from the lowest NUMA scheduling domain, evaluates the preferred node first using fault benefits and node summaries, and extends to other nodes when unsatisfied or when the group spans multiple nodes.

Concurrent threshold and rate windows rely on atomic compare exchange so losers skip updates, and current task observation must handle exiting kernel threads, missing address spaces and self selection due to preemption.
Millisecond time differences and masked access intervals wrap safely, while migration flag races are resolved by alternate CPU search rather than blocking.
